synopsis: Southborough boards addressed major project funding, property redevelopment, and town anniversary celebrations during the week of October 12, 2026. The Golf Committee finalized its strategy for Special Town Meeting to secure Community Preservation Act funding for course irrigation and allocated revolving funds to pursue Audubon certification. The Board of Health approved a septic variance enabling a commercial property on Breakneck Hill Road to convert into a single-family home. Meanwhile, the Tricentennial Committee executed a contract for a 200-drone light show to kick off Southborough's 300th anniversary and advanced plans for an expanded summer music festival.

highlights.title: Irrigation funding strategy finalized for Special Town Meeting
highlights.why: The Golf Committee coordinated outreach and decided not to seek floor amendments for a warrant article requesting new and extended CPA funds plus revolving funds for course irrigation. The measure seeks to extend $550,000 previously approved, request approximately $350,000 in new CPA funding, and spend $100,000 from the revolving fund.

highlights.title: Contract signed for 200-drone Tricentennial light show
highlights.why: A contract was executed with Firefly for a 15-minute drone light show on January 1, 2027, launched from St. Mark's field with viewing at Woodward School and the Town House. Organizers are reevaluating a proposed community bonfire and horse-drawn rides due to cost and site constraints.

highlights.title: Septic variance approved for Breakneck Hill Road conversion
highlights.why: The Board of Health approved an 85-foot wetland setback variance for an upgraded nitrogen-reducing septic system at 66 Breakneck Hill Road. The approval allows the property to convert from commercial use to a four-bedroom single-family residence, contingent on Conservation Commission review.

highlights.title: Revolving funds approved for Audubon golf certification
highlights.why: The Golf Committee voted to pay $500 in membership dues and authorized up to $4,500 in revolving funds to hire a consultant for Audubon International environmental certification. The vote covers the shortfall between an $18,400 bid and available CPA funds.

highlights.title: Planning advances for Summer Nights 2027 music festival
highlights.why: Organizers are preparing to expand the town's annual Summer Nights event into a large-scale music festival on August 21, 2027, featuring multiple stages at Neary School grounds. The committee is finalizing an agreement with a headlining act and submitting a grant application for accessibility features.
